doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

title: Hearing Brubeck's Time Out and joining the Brubeck Brothers
summary: Lamb had no hesitation joining the Brubeck Brothers; he first heard Time Out on headphones from Jon Margolis.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Was there any hesitation on your part when the opportunity to join the Brubeck Brothers came up?
Okay. How familiar were you with Dave Brubeck’s music?

He was one of the first guys I heard jazz-wise. The drummer I was referring to back in the early days that my brother John brought down from Columbia was a super audiophile dude and he would turn us on to stuff, you know Pharoah Sanders, McCoy and all this stuff. But I had been playing piano for maybe a year but it was happening pretty quickly for me and I remember I was at the piano doing stuff and Jon Margolis, he’s the drummer from Dry Jack, right, he had a reel to reel tape recorder and he came up with these headphones and he put them on, he just put them on me, and it was the “Time Out” record. And I had never heard — I hadn’t heard a lot of stuff but that in particular was, “What is this?” The sound of it, the sound of the drums, the vibe of it you know, so I was a Brubeck fan in two seconds.
